current.text: Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa. The projected starters are Young, Kyshawn George, Dybantsa, Davis and Sarr.
Davis is expected to play center on offense. Sarr is expected to play more power forward, further from the basket, and to switch onto the perimeter on defense.
His usage should drop. With Young, Davis and Dybantsa he becomes the fourth or fifth offensive option, and a usage increase is hard to see.
His minutes should go up, but he will touch the ball less per minute.
Next to Davis he should get fewer rim contests, so his blocks and rebounds are expected to fall.
Playing further from the basket should mean more threes and a lower FG%.
Experts call his Yahoo rank of 56 too high and advise against drafting him in the 50s or 60s. Around pick 80 to 90 is a fair price.
In one 9-cat mock draft he went at pick 83.
He is coming back from a broken foot and surgery. He was only a partial participant in camp.
He should be ready for opening night.
Washington is likely to keep Davis, but a trade is possible. If Davis is traded, Sarr starts at center.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so late-season rest and minutes cuts are not expected.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under heavy pressure to win this season.

durable.text: He led the league in shots contested at the rim per game by a wide margin and piles up blocks.
Blocks are his standout category, far above the league pool.
His FG% is much better when he plays near the rim and takes fewer threes.
Injury history: a broken foot that needed surgery.

note: The experts agree Sarr is a fade at his Yahoo price (rank 56, value 18 USD). Young, Davis and Dybantsa cut his usage, and Davis cuts into the rim contests behind his elite blocks. Their fair price is closer to pick 80 to 90, which fits his average costs of about 4 to 5 USD and the 9 USD he went for in our league last season, so he is a fine blocks pickup in that range but not at 18 USD. Early in the season, check whether Davis really plays center, whether Sarr keeps blocking near 2 a game, whether his FG% falls as he takes more threes, and how his foot holds up.
